items: [main] **Declare the mode first.** `drive` runs the loop to merge-ready ("babysit this", "get it green"). `background` triages without blocking, for a plan still executing. `threads-only` answers review comments and touches nothing else. `check` is one status pass and a report ("check on X", "is it green"). Undeclared defaults to `drive`; a small or docs-only PR gets `check`. Use `gh` for view, checks, threads and merge

[main] **Work the merge frontier and nothing above it.** The lowest unmerged PR is the only one that matters until it merges. Upstack threads get read and batched, never fixed at the cost of restarting the frontier's checks. Caught upstack while the frontier is red? Go back down
[main] **One babysitter per stack.** Check nothing else is already on it before starting

[main] **Never mutate stack topology.** No base retarget, rebase, stack-wide submit or force-push from inside a babysit. Fix on the owning branch and report anything rebase-shaped upward for the owner to do

[main] **Order is conflicts, then review threads, then CI.** Batch every known fix into one push wave. A conflict is the one blocker you report rather than resolve: say which branch needs the rebase and stop. Name the drift sweep in that report, since trunk may have grown callers of code the stack deletes or moves

[main] **Trust the forge's verdict, not a green check list.** Ready means `gh` agrees the PR can merge. Watch with `gh pr checks <N> --watch`, then re-read the PR and threads. Stop `drive` at a merge-ready frontier: checks green and `gh pr view <N> --json state,mergeable,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup` reporting mergeable with no blockers. Do not leave the watcher running until merges happen; that is `pb-land`. A watcher re-arm never authorizes merging or arming merge-when-ready

[main] **Classify CI before any retrigger.** Flake or infrastructure earns one fresh build, never a job retry, and only one. An identical second failure was never flake: reclassify and read the child logs. A failure in code the diff never touches means a stale base, so check `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before assuming flake and report it as needing a rebase instead of burning retries. Only a failure in the diff's own code gets a commit

[main] **Triage every review comment skeptically.** Verify each claim against the code. Each comment: fix it, dismiss it with a concrete reason, or ask. Fix real findings with a red-first proof in the lowest PR that owns the code, never at the tip unless the owning PR has merged. Push the fix wave before replying so the reply cites the commit. Reply with `gh api --method POST "repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<pr>/comments/<comment-id>/replies" --input <payload.json>`, putting the reply body in the JSON file as data and never interpolating comment text into a shell command. From the third pass on, lean toward dismissing documented patterns, still escalating anything touching security, auth, billing, data or migrations rather than dismissing it yourself. Never churn code to quiet a bot

[main] **Stop at the human's line.** Owner approval is a wait, not a blocker to fix. Babysitting never authorizes merging: only an explicit request to merge, land, ship, or merge when ready does, and that routes to `pb-land`. Surface the escalation and keep working the rest. When the frontier is merge-ready, sweep the run's triage decisions once and offer any team-useful dismissal pattern as a candidate rubric entry with its own PR rather than keeping it in private memory
